answer: Stop sybils with a mirror bond on a shared meadow. Each identity locks one bond and must complete a voyage: a sequential, memory-hard walk whose checkpoints mirror the bonds of unrelated peers, so one walk cannot be copied or run in parallel. Clones from one funder share a single mirror: their bonds reflect each other and collapse into one standing, while the k-th clone pays k squared in bond. A meadow holds only so many walkers, so late clones wait outside while honest agents cross.
